Sacrum is the broad eft of all the Bones of the Back, and doth sustain all the other Vertebra on the Inside. it is smooth and hollow, on the outside, convex, and uneven, being of something a triangular, shape. symphysis.c: SYMPHYSIS, is the joyning of two Bones, of which neither has a proper distinct Motion: This is either without any Medium, or else with it, as with a Cartilage, or Grifle, a Ligament, or Flesh, Cc.

symptom.c: SYMPTOM, is a preternatural Disposition of the Body, occasion'd by some Disease; this is either a Disease caused by another Disease; or else the Cause of a Disease proceeding from another Disease; or else simply a Symptom: This last is either some Action of the Body hindred, or disturbed, some Fault of the Excrement, or change of the natural Temper: Blanchard.:

shes.c: SHES. Rondeletius distinguishes Sithes, from the Places where they are found, into Sea Fish, River Fish, and Lake or Pond Fish; and of these he makes some other Subdivisions. But Mr. Wi is lough by faith rightly, That Sis bes are much bet - ter divided by 4 aristotle into these three Kinds, Cetaceous, Cartilaginous, and Spinous, The Cetaceons Kind ( which are: sometimes therefore call'd the Bellie Marine) have Lungs and Breath like Quadrupeds, they copulate also like - them, conceive and bring forth their Young alive, whom they suckle with their Milk. The Cartslaginous Sort, are produc'd from large Eggs like Birds, which are excluded the Womb also like those of Birds, The Spinous Kind, are also Oviparous, but their Eggs are smaller, and they have Spine up and down in their Flesh ro strengthen it. But he thinks it would be yet. more proper to divide Sithes into the Cetaceous Kind, or such as breath with Lungs, and into such as breath with Gills. And then, to subdivide those that breath with Gills, not into Cartilaginous and Spinous, but into Viviparous and Oviparous. The Viviparous Kind, that breath with Gills, he subdivided into Long, such as the Galei, and Ca nes or Sharks, and Dog-Sis: And the Broad Kind; such as the Paftinace, Raj c, Squatine, &c. all whose Subdivisions he gives in his Chapter of Cartilaginous Fishes in general. The Oviparous Kind, that breath with Gills, are the most numerous; and these he subdivided into such as are what we usually call Flat Fish; and such as him with their Backs upright, or at Right Angles ro the Horizon, The Plain or Flat Sis Kind, called usually Plani Spin off, are either Quadrati, as the Rhomb and Passer es; or Longinfculi, as the Solee. Such as swim with their Backs ere; ate either Long and Smooth, and without Scales, as the Eel Kind; or Shorter and leis Smooth: And these have either but one Pair of Fins at their Gills, which are call'd Orbes and Congeneres; or else another Pair of Fins also on their Bellies. And this latter Kind he divides into two others; 1. Such as have no Prickly Fins on their Backs, bur Soft and Flexile ones.. Such as have Prickly Fins upon their Backs. SO OTE, was the general Word for a Popular Convention of all the Inhabitants of any Place; which if it were of those of a City or Town, it was called a Burgh-mote; but if of all the Free Tenants of a County, twas called a Schire-mote. In Towns and Burghs, this solemn Assembly was made by the of a Bell call'd the Mot bell. In the County Folk-mote, all Knights and Free Tenants did their Fealty to the King, and elected their annual Sheriff formerly, ( on the ft of O over) before the King nominated. Bot after that, ( about the Time of Edward IL.) the City Folk-mote was changed into the Common-Council, and the County Folk mote into the Sheriffs Turn and Affifes. The Word Folk-mote had also sometimes a less Excent, signifying only the Assembly of the Tenants to a Court Leet or Baron of their Lord,
